original_content.problem:
Which of the following are linear differential operators?

Select all that apply.
original_content.worked_solution:
For any linear differential operator,

$$
D(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2})=aD({y}_{1})+bD({y}_{2})
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants. 

Let's check each case in turn.

- The first operator is indeed linear. To see this, we check the above linearity condition:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{1}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2}) & ={x}^{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2})+{x}^{2}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2}) \\  & =a{x}^{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+b{x}^{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+a{x}^{2}{y}_{1}+a{x}^{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =a\left[{x}^{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{x}^{2}{y}_{1}\right]+b\left[{x}^{3}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{x}^{2}{y}_{2}\right] \\  & =a{D}_{1}({y}_{1})+b{D}_{1}({y}_{2})\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operator is **not** linear.
To see why, we first evaluate the left-hand side of the linearity condition:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{2}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2}) & =(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2})\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2})+2(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2}) \\  & =(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2})\left(a\frac{\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}x}+b\frac{\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}x}\right)+2a{y}_{1}+2b{y}_{2} \\  & ={a}^{2}{y}_{1}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}x}+{b}^{2}{y}_{2}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}x}+ab\left({y}_{1}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}x}+{y}_{2}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}x}\right)+2a{y}_{1}+2b{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is not the same as the right-hand side, because

$$
\begin{aligned}a{D}_{2}({y}_{1})+b{D}_{2}({y}_{2}) & =a\left[{y}_{1}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}x}+2{y}_{1}\right]+b\left[{y}_{2}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}x}+2{y}_{2}\right] \\  & =a{y}_{1}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}x}+b{y}_{2}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}x}+2a{y}_{1}+2b{y}_{2}.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- The third operator is also linear. To see this, we check the above linearity condition:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{3}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2})+x(a{y}_{1}+b{y}_{2}) \\  & =a\frac{\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}x}+b\frac{\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}x}+ax{y}_{1}+bx{y}_{2} \\  & =a\left[\frac{\text{d}{y}_{1}}{\text{d}x}+x{y}_{1}\right]+b\left[\frac{\text{d}{y}_{2}}{\text{d}x}+x{y}_{2}\right] \\  & =a{D}_{3}({y}_{1})+b{D}_{3}({y}_{2})\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
